notes: Overall a solid implementation with clean structure, but has notable violations and gaps. Architectural: The Event Bus is used correctly for task.assigned, task.statusChanged, and comment.added. Services own their own data stores. HTTP handling is centralized in router.ts. However, the router directly calls services.tasks.getById() and services.users.getById() inside the comment creation handler to extract taskTitle, authorName, and assigneeId before passing them to CommentService — this is a cross-service data access violation. The comment.added event payload is enriched by the router with data from other services' domains rather than each service being truly autonomous. This is a design smell that violates the 'each service owns its data exclusively' rule in spirit, even if not a direct service-to-service call. Completeness: All five services are present. Full CRUD is implemented for users, projects, tasks, and comments. Add/remove members works. Task assignment and status transitions are implemented. Notifications respond to all three required events. A demo script is included and exercises the full flow. Missing: no unsubscribe mechanism on EventBus, no GET /tasks without projectId (minor), no way to get all notifications (minor). Status transition allows no-op same-status return which is debatable. Constraint compliance issues: (1) Router accesses two service stores (users, tasks) to enrich comment creation payload — indirect but real coupling through the router layer. (2) The comment.added notification for assigneeId relies on the router passing assigneeId fetched from TaskService, meaning CommentService and NotificationService cannot function independently without the router doing this bridging — this workaround papers over the architectural problem rather than solving it cleanly (the event should carry enough context from TaskService via the bus, but TaskService doesn't know about comments). The cleanest solution would have CommentService publish the event with just taskId/authorId and NotificationService either be fed the assigneeId via the event (which requires TaskService to publish a richer event), or accept that the comment.added event is incomplete. Code quality: TypeScript types are used well, error handling is present, the EventBus swallows subscriber errors gracefully, UUID generation is clean, HTTP parsing is robust. Minor issue: sendJSON with 204 sends an empty JSON object '{}' rather than no body. The router's URL matching logic using endsWith('/status') and endsWith('/assign') is fragile and could match unintended routes. DELETE /projects/:id incorrectly matches before the /members route check due to ordering — actually on review the members regex check is placed after the DELETE handler for projects, so DELETE /projects/:id/members would be caught by the projects DELETE handler extracting only parts[2] which is the project id, not the members sub-path — this is a routing bug. Overall a competent implementation that loses points primarily for the cross-service data leakage through the router and the routing order bug.
